grammatical_complexity.notes: Dominated by past simple narrative with dialogue in present simple. Past perfect, present perfect, and conditional structures appear as a noticeable minority. Relative clauses and participial constructions recur throughout. No highly advanced structures like third conditionals or inversion.

references_found: Seattle vs Boise US geography and political stereotypes
mandatory anti-racism training in corporate settings
Washington Post and CNN as US media references
US salary and benefits structure ($50K-$100K, medical/dental, paid vacation)
cultural_reference_load.notes: The entire plot hinges on understanding US racial politics, corporate diversity culture, and the progressive-vs-conservative cultural divide. A Latin American learner would likely miss the significance of the African-American correction, the anti-racism training concept, and the open-carry gun culture without specific US cultural knowledge.

sentence_structure.notes: Mixed lengths throughout. Dialogue lines are short (3-10 words) while narrative sentences range from 15-25 words with some compound and complex structures. Subordinate clauses appear regularly but do not dominate.

items.context: No, it's actually in South America.
items.reason: Used in the English sense of 'in fact' which differs from Spanish 'actualmente' (currently). A Spanish speaker may momentarily confuse it, though context (correcting a geographic misconception) makes the intended meaning recoverable.

items.context: Alejandra grabbed her bags and headed to the exit.
items.reason: Context of an airport makes 'way out' the obvious meaning. Spanish 'éxito' (success) would make no sense here.

items.context: As the taxi driver made his way to the interview location
items.reason: Clearly means 'place' in this context. The Spanish meaning 'locación' (renting) would not fit.

items.context: once you take the training, your eyes will be opened
items.reason: Used as 'as soon as/when' which is very different from Spanish 'once' (eleven). A Spanish speaker could be momentarily confused, though the sentence structure makes 'eleven' nonsensical.

items.context: This here is 20 years of following proper grazing principles.
items.reason: Means 'correct/appropriate' which is close enough to the Spanish 'propio' in some contexts, and the surrounding context of grazing principles makes the meaning clear.

items.context: she had spent the past few years working hard to prove to the world
items.reason: Context of hard work and demonstrating capability makes 'demonstrate' the clear meaning, not Spanish 'probar' (to try/taste).

items.context: God has given me a lot of success over the years.
items.reason: Context of achievement and God's blessings makes 'success' clearly mean accomplishment, not Spanish 'suceso' (event/occurrence).
